name: Total Revenue Across Regions
description: Aggregate revenue across a domestic and an international region, with currency and unit conversion.
formula: Total Revenue (USD) = Domestic Revenue + (International Revenue (local currency) × FX Rate). At advanced difficulty, a third region reports volume in cases rather than units: Region 3 Revenue = (Cases Sold × Units per Case) × Price per Unit, added to the total.
business_contexts: a boutique furniture maker closing out its first full year of international online sales
a consumer electronics brand totaling revenue across its US and European storefronts
a wholesale distributor totaling a completed shipping cycle across multiple regions
a specialty foods company combining domestic revenue with sales from its export distributor, who reports in cases rather than individual units
a subscription meal-kit company closing its books for the quarter across two currency zones
question_patterns: What was the client's total revenue in dollars, once the international region is converted?
Before subtracting anything, what was the total amount the client collected from customers across all regions, in dollars?
What figure lands on the very first line of the client's consolidated income statement for this period?
Once cases are converted to units and everything is converted to dollars, what was total revenue?
solution_logic: Step 1: Convert international revenue = international_revenue_foreign × fx_rate
Step 2: Calculate total revenue = domestic_revenue + converted international revenue
Step 1 (advanced): Convert region 3 volume to units = region3_cases_sold × region3_units_per_case
Step 2 (advanced): Calculate region 3 revenue = converted units × region3_price_per_unit
Step 3 (advanced): Convert international revenue = international_revenue_foreign × fx_rate
Step 4 (advanced): Calculate total revenue = domestic_revenue + converted international revenue + region 3 revenue
key_insight: Revenue isn't ready to add up until every region is on the same footing — the same currency and the same unit of volume.
common_mistakes: Adding the foreign-currency figure directly without converting it to dollars first
Adding cases directly to a unit-based price instead of converting cases to units first
Subtracting costs before arriving at revenue, which conflates revenue with profit
framework_soundbite: Revenue is price times quantity — but first, get every region onto the same currency and the same unit.
